## How to query files that communicate with a specific IP

### 1. Build the request URL

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files
```

### 2. Set the HTTP headers

```http
Accept: application/json
x-apikey: my_api
```

### 3. Add query parameters

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `limit`   | `10`  | Maximum number of results to return (the API’s default is 4). |
| `cursor`  | `pointer` | Continuation cursor for pagination (if you’re continuing from a previous page). |

So the full request would look like:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor=pointer
Accept: application/json
x-apikey: my_api
```

### 4. Parse the response

The JSON response will contain a `data` array with file objects and a `links` object that may include a `next` link containing the next cursor value. Example snippet:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "file_id_1",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
    "self": "...",
    "next": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?cursor=next_pointer"
  }
}
```

If you need more than 10 results, you can follow the `next` link and keep retrieving until you’ve collected all the data you need.

---

## Quick Python example

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files"
headers = {
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "x-apikey": "my_api"
}
params = {
    "limit": 10,
    "cursor": "pointer"
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(response.json())
```

Replace `"my_api"` with your actual API key. If you hit rate limits or need to paginate, just loop over the `next` link.
